entities.profile: Lenders and deposit takers handling customer, borrower and employee data.

entities.name: Insurers and insurance intermediaries
entities.profile: Life, general and health insurers, brokers, corporate agents, TPAs and web aggregators.

entities.name: Securities market entities
entities.profile: Stock brokers, depository participants, AMCs, AIFs, registrars and market infrastructure.

updates.title: Consent Manager registration opens under the DPDP Act
updates.ref: s. 6(9) and s. 27(1)(d) of the Act; rule 4 of the DPDP Rules, 2025
updates.applies: Companies that want to register as Consent Managers, and Data Fiduciaries that plan to accept consent through them.
changes: Rule 4 and the First Schedule apply from 13-11-2026: an Indian company with net worth of at least Rs 2 crore and an independently certified platform may apply to the Board.
The Board may inquire into a breach of a Consent Manager's registration conditions (s. 27(1)(d)).
The duties of Data Fiduciaries on notice, consent, security and breaches still start on 13-05-2027.

lender.text: Decide whether to onboard to Consent Manager platforms once they are registered.

actions: Track which Consent Managers the Board registers and publishes on its website.

updates.title: DPDP (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2026 adjusts the wording of ss. 9(1) and 10(2)(c)(ii)
updates.applies: Data Fiduciaries processing data of children or persons with disability, and Significant Data Fiduciaries.
changes: s. 9(1) now refers to the personal data of a child or of a person with disability who has a lawful guardian.
s. 10(2)(c)(ii) now requires a periodic data audit.
No change to the commencement dates.

lender.text: Read the amended wording when designing guardian consent flows.

sdf.text: The periodic audit is a data audit.

updates.title: Applications invited for the Chairperson and four Members of the Data Protection Board
updates.applies: The Data Protection Board of India.
changes: The Ministry invited applications for one Chairperson and four Members, with applications closing on 06-07-2026.
The Board was established on 13-11-2025 and its strength fixed at four Members besides the Chairperson; appointments are made on the recommendation of search-cum-selection committees under rule 17.

lender.text: No direct duty; the Board's inquiries and penalties begin on 13-05-2027.

updates.title: Corrigendum to the DPDP Rules, 2025
changes: Corrects wording errors in the Rules as published. The commencement periods are unchanged.

updates.title: DPDP Rules, 2025 notified; Act brought into force in three phases; Data Protection Board established
updates.applies: Every Data Fiduciary, including banks, NBFCs, insurers, intermediaries and market entities, and their processors.
changes: Phase 1 (13-11-2025): definitions, the Board, the rule-making and overriding provisions, and the RTI Act amendment; rules 1, 2 and 17 to 21.

Phase 3 (13-05-2027): notice, consent, legitimate uses, security, breach intimation, retention, children, Significant Data Fiduciaries, rights, transfers abroad, exemptions, Board inquiries and penalties; omission of IT Act s. 43A.
The Board is set up with its head office in the National Capital Region, and the number of its Members is fixed at four.

lender.text: Eighteen months to build notices, consent flows, breach playbooks with a 72-hour Board report, retention and erasure, and rights handling.

insurer.text: Same, including proposal-form consent and intermediary contracts.

securities.text: Same, alongside the CSCRF incident and data localisation rules.

sdf.text: Prepare for a Data Protection Officer, independent data audits and yearly impact assessments if notified.

processor.text: Expect new contract clauses on security safeguards, breach reporting, logs and erasure.

actions: Map personal data held and the lawful ground for each use.
Redesign notices and consent records so consent can be proved (s. 6(10)).
Build a breach response that reports to the Board without delay and within 72 hours, alongside RBI, SEBI or IRDAI and CERT-In six-hour reports.
Set retention schedules that reconcile erasure with KYC, PMLA and sector record-keeping laws.
Update processor contracts for rule 6 safeguards.
